## How the score was worked out

Each result implies a score on its own, after adjusting for how hard that test is and who ran it. The model's score is their weighted average, with a small pull toward the middle for thinly tested models. Each test's weight is its *counts* column above; here it is added up by who ran the tests. ## How to run it

### Other ways to run it

1. Run it as published (BF16, needs ~148 GB, NVIDIA only, from [huggingface.co/nvidia](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-74B-A9B-BF16/blob/567021037ff88364143e24ea05e6abd0f72086ff/README.md))
   
   ```sh
   wget https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-74B-A9B-BF16/resolve/main/ultra_v3_reasoning_parser.py
   
   export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
   
   vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-74B-A9B-BF16 \
     --trust-remote-code \
     --load-format auto \
     --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
     --max-model-len 262144 \
     --max-num-seqs 1 \
     --enable-chunked-prefill \
     --attention-backend FLASHINFER \
     --mamba-backend flashinfer \
     --mamba-cache-mode align \
     --seed 42 \
     --allowed-local-media-path / \
     --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"video":1,"image":1}' \
     --video-pruning-rate 0.5 \
     --media-io-kwargs '{"video":{"fps":2,"num_frames":256}}' \
     --enable-auto-tool-choice \
     --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
     --reasoning-parser-plugin ultra_v3_reasoning_parser.py \
     --reasoning-parser ultra_v3
   ```

Official weights and documentation: [huggingface.co/nvidia](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-74B-A9B-BF16)
